original_question: Do there exist metrically non-isomorphic measure-preserving dynamical systems that nevertheless have the same continuous spectrum, in particular the same Lebesgue spectrum?
target_in_paper: Section 1, opening unnumbered spectral problem: whether there exist metrically different dynamical systems with one and the same continuous (in particular, Lebesgue) spectrum. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core content almost verbatim: it is an existence question about two measure-preserving systems, asks for metric non-isomorphism, and focuses on coincidence of continuous spectrum, highlighting the Lebesgue case. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
missing_details: The paper states this as an unnumbered opening problem in §1, not as Banach's problem Q2 or the weakened Banach problem Q4; those neighboring questions concern existence of a single automorphism with prescribed spectral type, not two non-isomorphic systems with the same spectrum. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

To make the question stand-alone in the paper's ambient setting, dynamical systems should be read as measure-preserving automorphisms of probability spaces (the note's main setting is a single automorphism, i.e. a Z-action). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03641))

Metrically non-isomorphic should be made explicit as non-isomorphic as measure-preserving systems mod 0. This is implicit in the paper's ergodic-theoretic usage. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

Same continuous spectrum should be tied to the spectrum of the associated Koopman operator; otherwise same spectrum is under-specified for a stand-alone question. The paper does not further formalize multiplicity at this point, so the refined version should not add extra spectral restrictions not stated there. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

The sentence about ergodic automorphisms of compact commutative groups is only context describing where the author searched for examples; it is not part of the problem's formal scope and should not be inserted as a hypothesis. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
refined_question: Do there exist two measure-preserving automorphisms of probability spaces that are not metrically isomorphic mod 0 but whose Koopman operators have one and the same continuous spectrum, and in particular one and the same Lebesgue spectrum?
justification: This draft is targeting the very first problem raised in §1, stated in the opening paragraph before Q1. It is the paper's broad spectral-comparison question and not one of the later numbered Banach-type existence questions. Q2 asks for a single automorphism with simple Lebesgue spectrum, and Q4 asks for a single automorphism with finite-multiplicity absolutely continuous spectrum; neither matches your two-system comparison. The author's mention of ergodic automorphisms of compact commutative groups merely records the class in which he tried to find examples. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
